q6.answer: The server keeps an applied-changes record per user and change id, holding the result it returned and the sequence number. A retry with a change id it has already handled gets the stored result back and nothing new is written, because the change's note update, log entry and applied-changes record commit together.

q7.answer: The phone keeps the download cursor (the last applied log sequence number) in its local sync state. It moves only in the same local transaction that applies a download page, so the page and the cursor are saved together or not at all.

q8.answer: The phone's local transaction for that page never commits, so the cursor stays at its old value. The next sync re-downloads from that cursor, and replaying entries is safe because each entry carries a full body and version and is applied only if its version is higher than the one stored.

q9.answer: The upload response tells the losing phone its change was a conflict, with the current note version and the conflict note's id, and the phone removes that queue row only after storing that result. The winning text reaches its copy of the original note through the next download, which applies the winning log entry (and the conflict note arrives the same way), so the phone converges with the server via the change log rather than via the upload response. The design does not say whether the conflict response itself carries the winning body.

q10.answer: A queue row is removed only after the phone has received and stored the server's result for it, either accepted or conflict, which is the step after the upload response. If the response never arrives, the row stays in flight and the retry with the same change id is what resolves it.

q11.answer: The download updates only the stored server version of the note and leaves the displayed text alone, so the user's unsent edit stays visible. The pending change keeps its original base version, since the base lives in the queue row, so the later upload will be judged by the server against the newer version and will likely conflict.

q12.answer: The new edit does not fold into the in-flight row. It goes into a new queue row for that note and waits, because only one change per note is in flight at a time. If the earlier change is accepted, the waiting row's base becomes the version the server returned for it; if the earlier change conflicts, the waiting row keeps its old base and the server judges it.
